claim: Arginine methyltransferase PRMT7 is associated with human breast cancer metastasis.
source: Arginine methyltransferase PRMT7 is associated with human breast cancer metastasis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established association, drawing on prior knowledge in the field.

claim: Endosomal FAK signalling is critical for cancer cell migration.
source: Endosomal FAK signalling is critical for cancer cell migration.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about FAK signaling's role in cancer cell migration.

claim: PRMT7 promotes endosomal FAK signalling activation during breast cancer metastasis.
source: Here we identified the pivotal roles of PRMT7 in promoting endosomal FAK signalling activation during breast cancer metastasis.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: PRMT7 binds to scaffold protein SHANK2.
source: PRMT7 exerted its functions through binding to scaffold protein SHANK2
evidence: This is supported by CoIP assays shown in Figure 1B and C, and GST pull-down assays in Figure 1D.

claim: PRMT7 catalyzes di-methylation of SHANK2 at R240.
source: PRMT7 exerted its functions through binding to scaffold protein SHANK2 and catalyzing di-methylation of SHANK2 at R240.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 2A and methylation assays in Figures 1G-J and 2C-E.

claim: SHANK2 R240 methylation exposes ANK domain by disrupting its SPN-ANK domain blockade.
source: SHANK2 R240 methylation exposed ANK domain by disrupting its SPN-ANK domain blockade
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulations shown in Figure 4, demonstrating conformational changes.

claim: SHANK2 R240 methylation promotes co-accumulation of dynamin2, talin, FAK, and cortactin with SHANK2 on endosomes.
source: SHANK2 R240 methylation exposed ANK domain by disrupting its SPN-ANK domain blockade, promoting in co-accumulation of dynamin2, talin, FAK, cortactin with SHANK2 on endosomes.
evidence: This is supported by CoIP assays in Figure 5 and immunofluorescence data showing co-localization.

claim: SHANK2 R240 methylation activates endosomal FAK/cortactin signals in vitro.
source: In addition, SHANK2 R240 methylation activated endosomal FAK/cortactin signals in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data showing increased phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin in Figures 6A-F.

claim: SHANK2 R240 methylation activates endosomal FAK/cortactin signals in vivo.
source: In addition, SHANK2 R240 methylation activated endosomal FAK/cortactin signals in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by xenograft mouse model data in Figure 8, showing increased phosphorylation in tumor tissues.

claim: PRMT7 levels correlate with aggressive clinical breast cancer tissues.
source: Consistently, all the levels of PRMT7, methylated SHANK2, FAK Y397 phosphorylation and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation were correlated with aggressive clinical breast cancer tissues.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data from patient samples shown in Figure 8E-F.

claim: Methylated SHANK2 levels correlate with aggressive clinical breast cancer tissues.
source: Consistently, all the levels of PRMT7, methylated SHANK2, FAK Y397 phosphorylation and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation were correlated with aggressive clinical breast cancer tissues.
evidence: This is supported by western blot analysis of patient samples in Figure 3B-E.

claim: FAK Y397 phosphorylation levels correlate with aggressive clinical breast cancer tissues.
source: Consistently, all the levels of PRMT7, methylated SHANK2, FAK Y397 phosphorylation and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation were correlated with aggressive clinical breast cancer tissues.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data from patient samples shown in Figure 8E-F.

claim: Cortactin Y421 phosphorylation levels correlate with aggressive clinical breast cancer tissues.
source: Consistently, all the levels of PRMT7, methylated SHANK2, FAK Y397 phosphorylation and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation were correlated with aggressive clinical breast cancer tissues.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data from patient samples shown in Figure 8E-F.

claim: PRMTs catalyze mono-methylation and symmetric or asymmetric di-methylation of arginine residues on both histone and non-histone substrates.
source: Protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMTs) catalyze mono-methylation and symmetric or asymmetric di-methylation of arginine residues on both histone and non-histone substrates to modulate diverse biological processes
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations (Jelinic et al., 2006; Bedford and Clarke, 2009; Dhar et al., 2012; Jeong et al., 2016; Blanc and Richard, 2017; Jeong et al., 2020).

claim: PRMT7 was reported as a type III PRMT to catalyze mono-methylation of arginine residues on both histone and non-histone substrates.
source: Protein Arginine Methyltransferase 7 (PRMT7) was reported as a type III PRMT to catalyze mono-methylation of arginine residues on both histone and non-histone substrates
evidence: This is supported by citations (Bedford and Clarke, 2009; Karkhanis et al., 2012; Blanc and Richard, 2017; Jain and Clarke, 2019; Haghandish et al., 2019).

claim: PRMT7 can symmetrically di-methylate proteins such as p38 and GLI2.
source: Recent studies also reported that PRMT7 can symmetrically di-methylate proteins such as p38 and GLI2
evidence: This is supported by citations (Jeong et al., 2020; Vuong et al., 2020).

claim: PRMT7 promoted metastasis of breast carcinoma cells by triggering EMT program.
source: Specifically, our previous work reported that PRMT7 promoted metastasis of breast carcinoma cells by triggering EMT (epithelial-mesenchymal transition) program
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work (Yao et al., 2014).

claim: PRMT7 can upregulate the expression of matrix metalloproteinase nine to promote metastasis of breast cancer.
source: PRMT7 can also upregulate the expression of matrix metalloproteinase nine to promote metastasis of breast cancer
evidence: This is supported by citation (Baldwin et al., 2015).

claim: PRMT7 was automethylated at residue R531, which potentiated the PRMT7-induced EMT program and metastasis.
source: We also found that PRMT7 was automethylated at residue R531, which potentiated the PRMT7-induced EMT program and metastasis
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work (Geng et al., 2017).

claim: Endocytosis of migrating cells is a fundamental process which is required for adhesion formation and efficient cell movement.
source: Endocytosis of migrating cells is a fundamental process which is required for adhesion formation and efficient cell movement
evidence: This is supported by citations (Kaksonen and Roux, 2018; Scita and Di Fiore, 2010).

claim: Deregulated endocytosis contributes to the acquisition of malignant characteristics in tumour cells, including enhanced cell migration, invasion and metastasis.
source: Increasing evidence indicates that deregulated endocytosis is a relapse mechanism that contributes to the acquisition of malignant characteristics in tumour cells, including enhanced cell migration, invasion and metastasis
evidence: This is supported by citations (Hamidi and Ivaska, 2018; McMahon and Boucrot, 2011).

claim: FAK is a cytoplasmic protein-tyrosine kinase that plays a pivotal role in cell adhesion, survival and migration.
source: The focal adhesion kinase (FAK) is a cytoplasmic protein-tyrosine kinase and plays a pivotal role in many cellular processes such as cell adhesion, survival and migration
evidence: This is supported by citations (Murphy and Courtneidge, 2011; Alanko and Ivaska, 2016; Schoenherr et al., 2018).

claim: During endocytosis, integrin or talin engages with FAK to co-localize on endosome.
source: During endocytosis, integrin or talin engages with FAK to co-localize on endosome.
evidence: This is supported by citations (Alanko et al., 2015; Nader et al., 2016; Xiuping et al., 2018; Hamidi and Ivaska, 2018).

claim: FAK undergoes autophosphorylation on Y397, which results in cell dissemination.
source: FAK undergos autophosphorylation on Y397, which results in cell dissemination
evidence: This is supported by citations (Alanko et al., 2015; Nader et al., 2016; Xiuping et al., 2018; Hamidi and Ivaska, 2018).

claim: Y397 phosphorylation of FAK facilitates the association of FAK with actin-binding protein cortactin.
source: Additionally, Y397 phosphorylation of FAK facilitates the association of FAK with actin-binding protein cortactin, which renders cortactin function in formation of lamellipodia and filopodia
evidence: This is supported by citations (Tomar et al., 2012; Eke et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2011).

claim: SHANK2 localizes in cytoplasm and plays important roles in regulating synapse plasticity.
source: Scaffolding proteins SH3 and multiple ankyrin repeat domains 2 (SHANK2) localizes in cytoplasm and plays important roles in regulating synapse plasticity
evidence: This is supported by citations (Lee et al., 2010; Naisbitt et al., 1999; Sala et al., 2001; Sheng and Kim, 2000; Tu et al., 1999).

claim: SHANK family proteins have been linked to Autistic Spectrum Disorder.
source: SHANK family proteins have been linked to Autistic Spectrum Disorder
evidence: This is supported by citations (Lim et al., 1999; Mei et al., 2016; Monteiro and Feng, 2017; Yoon et al., 2017).

claim: Mutations in genes encoding SHANK family proteins often result in marked behavioural phenotypes in mice.
source: Mutations in genes encoding SHANK family proteins (SHANK1, 2 and 3) often result in marked behavioural phenotypes in mice
evidence: This is supported by citations (Mameza et al., 2013; Schmeisser et al., 2012; Won et al., 2012).

claim: SHANK1 and SHANK3 were reported to inhibit cell spreading, migration and invasion in cancer cells through sequestering active Rap1 and R-Ras.
source: SHANK1 and SHANK3 were reported to inhibit cell spreading, migration and invasion in cancer cells through sequestering active Rap1 and R-Ras
evidence: This is supported by citation (Lilja et al., 2017).

claim: SHANK2 is a new substrate of PRMT7.
source: In this study, we identified that SHANK2 was a new substrate of PRMT7.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 1A and methylation assays in Figures 1G-J.

claim: PRMT7 is associated with multiple proteins including SHANK2, MRPS23, Plectin1, SNRPB and ARHGAP32.
source: The results revealed that PRMT7 is associated with multiple proteins including SHANK2, MRPS23, Plectin1, SNRPB and ARHGAP32.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: PRMT7 and SHANK2 can interact with each other in vitro.
source: We then incubated the purified GST-tagged PRMT7 with SHANK2 protein, and the results showed that they could interact with each other
evidence: This is supported by GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The SHANK2 ANK, PDZ and SAM domains are responsible for the interaction between PRMT7 and SHANK2.
source: we expressed a series of truncated GST- SHANK2 (Figure 1E), and found that the SHANK2 ANK, PDZ and SAM domains were responsible for the interaction between PRMT7 and SHANK2
evidence: This is supported by domain mapping experiments shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: Overexpression of PRMT7 results in increased symmetric arginine di-methylation of SHANK2 in HEK293T cells.
source: By using methylation assay, we found that overexpression of PRMT7 resulted in increased symmetric arginine di-methylation of SHANK2 in HEK293T cells (low level of PRMT7)
evidence: This is supported by methylation assay data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: SHANK2 di-methylation level is reduced upon PRMT7 depletion in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: SHANK2 di-methylation level was reduced upon PRMT7 depletion, and the reduced di-methylation of SHANK2 was restored by the reconstituted expression of WT PRMT7 (PRMT7 WT) but not by mutant PRMT7 at its enzymatic domain (PRMT7 Mut) in MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: This is supported by methylation assay data shown in Figure 1H and I.

claim: Incubation of recombinant PRMT7 and SHANK2 with SAM gives rise to a remarkable increase in methylation of SHANK2.
source: Apparently, incubation of recombinant PRMT7 and SHANK2 gave rise to a remarkable increase in methylation of SHANK2 in the presence of SAM, while SHANK2 methylation was undetectable in the absence of SAM
evidence: This is supported by in vitro methylation assay data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The arginine 240 residue (R240) of SHANK2 is di-methylated.
source: We identified that the arginine 240 residue (R240) of SHANK2 was di-methylated
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The R240 residue of SHANK2 is evolutionarily conserved.
source: Using sequence homology comparison, we found that the R240 residue of SHANK2 is evolutionarily conserved
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Di-methylation level of SHANK2 R240K is lower when compared to SHANK2 WT in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: We found that di-methylation level of SHANK2 R240K was lower when compared to SHANK2 WT in MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: SHANK2 R240 di-methylation level increases with increasing doses of PRMT7 in HEK293T cells.
source: We then overexpressed increasing doses of PRMT7 in HEK293T cells, and we found that SHANK2 R240 di-methylation level was increased accordingly
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Dosage dependent expression of PRMT5 does not increase the di-methylation at SHANK2 R240.
source: We found that dosage dependent expression of PRMT5 did not increase the di-methylation at SHANK2 R240
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Overexpression of PRMT7 can increase SHANK2 di-methylation level even when PRMT5 activity is inhibited.
source: We found that even when PRMT5 activity was inhibited, overexpression of PRMT7 could still increase the SHANK2 di-methylation level both in HEK293T and MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Di-methylation of SHANK2 R240 is mainly mediated by PRMT7.
source: Thus, although PRMT5 and PRMT7 existed in the same complex, our data indicated that di-methylation of SHANK2 R240 was mainly mediated by PRMT7.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing PRMT5 does not methylate SHANK2 R240 and PRMT7 does.

claim: SHANK2 mRNA is highly expressed in human breast tumours.
source: Consistently, we also observed that SHANK2 mRNA was highly expressed in human breast tumours
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: SHANK2 methylation level is significantly higher in luminal B Her2(+) and Triple-negative breast cancer samples than in normal, luminal A and luminal B Her2(-) samples.
source: The results demonstrated that SHANK2 methylation level was significantly higher in luminal B Her2(+) and Triple-negative breast cancer samples, than that in normal, luminal A and luminal B Her2(-) samples
evidence: This is supported by western blot analysis of patient samples shown in Figure 3B–E.

claim: SHANK2 methylation is positively correlated with high metastatic potential in breast cancer.
source: which implicated a positive correlation between SHANK2 methylation and high metastatic potential
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that SHANK2 methylation is higher in more aggressive breast cancer subtypes.

claim: Among 1075 breast cancer patients, 10.5% of PRMT7 low-expression patients were stage III or IV, while 27.6% of PRMT7 high-expression patients were stage III or IV.
source: Among 1075 breast cancer patients, 89 out of 847 PRMT7 low-expression breast cancer patients were stage III or IV (10.5%), while 63 out of 228 PRMT7 high-expression breast cancer patients were stage III or IV (27.6%)
evidence: This is supported by TCGA database analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The expression of PRMT7 is positively correlated with the proportion of patients with stage III or IV breast cancer.
source: These data indicated that the expression of PRMT7 was positively correlated with the proportion of patients with stage III or IV breast cancer, which predicted poor prognosis.
evidence: This is inferred from the TCGA data showing higher proportion of advanced stage cancer in PRMT7 high-expression patients.

claim: High metastatic potential breast cancer cells (BT549 and MDA-MB-231) exhibit high SHANK2 di-methylation levels.
source: Out of 6 cell lines analyzed, high metastatic potential breast cancer cells (BT549 and MDA-MB-231) exhibited high SHANK2 di-methylation levels
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: Normal mammary epithelial cell (MCF10A) and low metastatic potential breast cancer cells (MCF7, BT474 and T47D) show relatively low SHANK2 di-methylation level.
source: whereas normal mammary epithelial cell (MCF10A), low metastatic potential breast cancer cell (MCF7, BT474 and T47D) showed relatively low SHANK2 di-methylation level
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: The epithelial marker ZO-1 is increased upon SHANK2 depletion in MDA-MB-231 and BT549 cells.
source: we found that the epithelial marker ZO-1 was increased, while the mesenchymal markers Fibronectin and N-cadherin were decreased upon SHANK2 depletion
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The mesenchymal markers Fibronectin and N-cadherin are decreased upon SHANK2 depletion in MDA-MB-231 and BT549 cells.
source: we found that the epithelial marker ZO-1 was increased, while the mesenchymal markers Fibronectin and N-cadherin were decreased upon SHANK2 depletion
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not SHANK2 R240K restores Fibronectin and N-cadherin expression in SHANK2-depleted cells.
source: meanwhile, ZO-1 expression was decreased while Fibronectin and N-cadherin expressions were restored by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K in MDA-MB-231 and BT549 cells
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: MMP2/MMP9 activation is inhibited by SHANK2 depletion.
source: In addition, MMP2/MMP9 activation was inhibited by SHANK2 depletion, while the inhibition was abrogated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: The migration/invasion capabilities of MDA-MB-231 cells are inhibited by SHANK2 depletion.
source: and the migration/invasion capabilities of MDA-MB-231 cells were also inhibited by SHANK2 depletion, and in both cases the inhibition was abrogated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K
evidence: This is supported by transwell assay data shown in Figure 3J and K.

claim: The SPN domain in Dimethyl R240 needs less energy to reach an 'open' state than that in SHANK2 WT and R240K.
source: As shown in Figure 4A, the SPN domain in Dimethyl R240 needs less energy to reach an 'open' state than that in SHANK2 WT and R240K, according to the free energy profile.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: R240 can form hydrogen bonds with its neighbouring residue H236.
source: R240 can form hydrogen bonds with its neighbouring residue H236 and by this R240 remotely influences the interactions between SPN and ANK via hydrogen bond network
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: R240 methylation dramatically decreases interactions between R240 and H236.
source: It indicates that R240 methylation dramatically decreased interactions between R240 and H236.
evidence: This is inferred from the molecular dynamics simulation data showing conformational changes.

claim: R240 methylation weakens the stability of the closed state of SHANK2.
source: It further weakened the stability of the closed state of SHANK2.
evidence: This is inferred from the molecular dynamics simulation data showing decreased hydrogen bonding.

claim: SHANK2 can interact with numerous endosome associate proteins, including β1-integrin, talin, FAK, EEA1, dynamin2, clathrin, AP2 and cortactin.
source: The mass spectrometric data showed that SHANK2 could interact with numerous endosome associate proteins, including β1-integrin, talin, FAK, EEA1, dynamin2, clathrin, AP2 and cortactin
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Talin, FAK, dynamin2, cortactin and SHANK2 are in the same complex in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: To test this hypothesis, we first verified the mass spec data by using CoIP assays and we confirmed that talin, FAK, dynamin2, cortactin and SHANK2 were in the same complex in MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: This is supported by CoIP assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Overexpression of PRMT7 promotes the co-precipitation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2 with cortactin in MCF7 cells.
source: We found that overexpression of PRMT7 promoted the co-precipitation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2 with cortactin in MCF7 cells
evidence: This is supported by CoIP assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The interaction of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2 with cortactin is reduced in PRMT7 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: and the interaction was reduced in PRMT7 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: This is supported by CoIP assay data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Overexpression of PRMT7 triggers an accumulation in the number of EEA1-positive endosomes with more talin, FAK, EEA1 and dynamin2 colocalization in MCF7 cells.
source: Additionally, overexpression of PRMT7 triggered an accumulation in the number of EEA1-positive endosomes with more talin, FAK, EEA1 and dynamin2 colocalization in MCF7 cells
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The colocalization of talin, FAK, EEA1 and dynamin2 is attenuated in PRMT7 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: and the colocalization was attenuated in PRMT7 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The formation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin is significantly increased by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K in SHANK2 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Consistently, the formation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin was significantly increased by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K in SHANK2 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: This is supported by CoIP assay data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: SHANK2 WT promotes the recruitment of EEA1-positive endosomes in MDA-MB-231 and BT549 cells.
source: Meanwhile, SHANK2 WT promoted the recruitment of EEA1-positive endosomes and the majority of SHANK2 was associated with endosome associate proteins, which was significantly reduced by SHANK2 R240K in MDA-MB-231 and BT549 cells
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The interaction of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin is enhanced by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240F but not of SHANK2 WT or SHANK2 R240K in MCF10A cells.
source: Consistent with this finding, the interaction of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin and the localization between talin, FAK, EEA1 and dynamin2 with endosome compartment was enhanced by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240F (as a methyl-mimic) but not of SHANK2 WT or SHANK2 R240K in MCF10A cells expressing low level of PRMT7
evidence: This is supported by CoIP and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5J and K.

claim: SHANK2 silencing partially reduces the formation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin complex in PRMT7-MCF7 cells.
source: SHANK2 silencing partially reduced the formation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin complex
evidence: This is supported by CoIP assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: SHANK2 silencing markedly decreases the interaction between talin and FAK in PRMT7-MCF7 cells.
source: and markedly decreased the interaction between talin and FAK
evidence: This is supported by CoIP assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Overexpression of PRMT7 markedly increases FAK and cortactin phosphorylation in MCF7 cells.
source: As expected, overexpression of PRMT7 markedly increased FAK and cortactin phosphorylation in MCF7 cells
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: PRMT7 depletion profoundly decreases FAK and cortactin phosphorylation in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: and PRMT7 depletion profoundly decreased FAK and cortactin phosphorylation in MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: FAK and cortactin are activated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K.
source: Consistently, FAK and cortactin were activated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Blocking FAK activation with FAK inhibitor GSK2256098 inhibits phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin upregulated by SHANK2 R240F in SHANK2 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Furthermore, blocking FAK activation with FAK inhibitor GSK2256098 did inhibit phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin upregulated by SHANK2 R240F in SHANK2 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: SHANK2 R240F or SHANK2 WT, but not SHANK2 R240K increases phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin in SHANK2 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Consistently, we found that SHANK2 R240F or SHANK2 WT, but not SHANK2 R240K increased phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin in SHANK2 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Treatment with dynasore greatly decreases SHANK2 R240F induced-phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Treatment with dynasore or silencing of EEA1 greatly decreased SHANK2 R240F induced-phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin in MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Silencing of EEA1 greatly decreases SHANK2 R240F induced-phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Treatment with dynasore or silencing of EEA1 greatly decreased SHANK2 R240F induced-phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin in MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Treatment with dynasore decreases PRMT7 induced-EMT program in MCF7 cells.
source: Indeed, treatment with dynasore decreased PRMT7 induced-EMT program and migration/invasion capabilities of MCF7 cells
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Treatment with dynasore decreases PRMT7 induced-migration/invasion capabilities of MCF7 cells.
source: Indeed, treatment with dynasore decreased PRMT7 induced-EMT program and migration/invasion capabilities of MCF7 cells
evidence: This is supported by transwell assay data shown in Figure 7B–C.

claim: EMT and cell migration/invasion are activated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240F or SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K in SHANK2-depleted MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Likewise, EMT and cell migration/invasion were activated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240F or SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K in SHANK2-depleted MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: This is supported by western blot and transwell assay data shown in Figure 7D–F.

claim: Dynasore dramatically inhibits the effects of SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT and cell migration/invasion.
source: To determine the functional role of SHANK2 R240 methylation is dependent on endocytosis, we treated SHANK2 R240F MDA-MB-231 cells with dynasore, and found that dynasore dramatically inhibited the effects of SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT and cell migration/invasion
evidence: This is supported by western blot and transwell assay data shown in Figure 7D–F.

claim: Knockdown of EEA1 markedly reduces SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT and cell migration/invasion.
source: Similarly, knockdown of EEA1 also markedly reduced SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT and cell migration/invasion
evidence: This is supported by western blot and transwell assay data shown in Figure 7G–I.

claim: FAK inhibitor GSK2256098 inhibits the effects of SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT and cell migration/invasion.
source: Since SHANK2 R240 methylation promotes cell migration/invasion through activating endosomal FAK signalling, we treated SHANK2 R240F MDA-MB-231 cells with FAK inhibitor GSK2256098, and found that GSK2256098 also inhibited the effects of SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT and cell migration/invasion
evidence: This is supported by western blot and transwell assay data shown in Figure 7J–L.

claim: Lung metastases and the number of metastatic pulmonary nodules are dramatically decreased by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240K, but not of SHANK2 WT or SHANK2 R240F in xenograft mouse models.
source: The results demonstrated that lung metastases and the number of metastatic pulmonary nodules were dramatically decreased by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240K, but not of SHANK2 WT or SHANK2 R240F
evidence: This is supported by in vivo xenograft data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Mice injected with SHANK2 R240F cells and treated with GSK2256098 form fewer lung metastatic foci than those injected with SHANK2 R240F alone.
source: We also discovered that the mice injected with SHANK2 R240F cells and treated with GSK2256098 formed fewer lung metastatic foci than that injected with SHANK2 R240F
evidence: This is supported by in vivo xenograft data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: SHANK2 R240F expression reinforces FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation in vivo.
source: In addition, immunohistochemistry staining results indicated that SHANK2 R240F expression reinforced FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 8C and D.

claim: SHANK2 R240F with GSK2256098 treatment profoundly inhibits SHANK2 R240F induced-FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation in vivo.
source: whereas SHANK2 R240F with GSK2256098 treatment profoundly inhibited SHANK2 R240F induced-FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 8C and D.

claim: There is a correlation among PRMT7, FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation levels, and the clinical aggressiveness of breast cancer.
source: Immunohistochemistry staining results revealed a correlation among PRMT7, FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation levels, and the clinical aggressiveness of breast cancer
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis of patient samples shown in Figure 8E,F and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: SHANK2 R240 methylation maintains endocytic activity.
source: In this study, we report a new substrate of PRMT7, the scaffold protein SHANK2, which is di-methylated at arginine 240 residue to maintain endocytic activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing SHANK2 methylation promotes endosome formation and FAK signaling.

claim: SHANK2 R240K methylation results in the accumulation of dynamin2, talin, FAK and cortactin on the endosome.
source: In particular, SHANK2 R240K methylation disturbs SPN-ANK domain blockade of SHANK2, thereby resulting in the accumulation of dynamin2, talin, FAK and cortactin on the endosome.
evidence: This is supported by CoIP and immunofluorescence data showing increased co-localization of these proteins.

claim: SHANK2 R240 methylation increases the migration of SHANK2-dependent breast cancer metastasis.
source: SHANK2 R240 methylation further activates endosomal FAK/cortactin signals, which increases the migration of SHANK2-dependent breast cancer metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by transwell migration/invasion assays and in vivo xenograft data.

claim: Methylated SHANK2 might be involved in clatharin-mediated endocytosis.
